introduction.text: Castel Sant'Angelo is a historic fortress and museum in Rome, originally built as Emperor Hadrian's mausoleum. Its strategic location on the Tiber and its evolution from mausoleum to papal fortress and prison make it a key monument in Roman history and culture.

history.description: Construction of the Mausoleum of Hadrian, a cylindrical rotunda commissioned by Emperor Hadrian to house his tomb and that of his family.
Transfer of Hadrian's ashes to the mausoleum a year after his death in 138 AD.
Inclusion of the mausoleum into the Aurelian Walls and its conversion into a military fortress in 401 AD.
Destruction of the mausoleum's contents during the Visigoth sacking of Rome in 410 AD.
Destruction of the mausoleum's bronze and stone statuary during the Gothic siege of Rome in 537 AD.
Legend of Archangel Michael appearing atop the mausoleum during the plague of 590 AD, leading to its renaming as Castel Sant'Angelo.
Conversion of the structure into a papal castle in the 14th century, including the construction of the Passetto di Borgo.
Use of the castle as a refuge during the Sack of Rome in 1527.
Installation of a marble statue of Saint Michael by Raffaello da Montelupo in 1536.
Replacement of Montelupo's statue with a bronze statue by Peter Anton von Verschaffelt in 1753.
Decommissioning of the castle as a fortress and its conversion into a museum in 1901.
The castle served as a prison for notable figures such as Giordano Bruno, Benvenuto Cellini, and Cagliostro.

design.description: The original mausoleum was a cylindrical rotunda with a garden top and a golden quadriga.
The Passetto di Borgo, a covered fortified corridor connecting the castle to St. Peter's Basilica, was added during the papal conversion.
The castle's interior includes a Treasury Room where the ashes of emperors were stored.
The castle's fortifications were reinforced during the 14th century to serve as a papal stronghold.
The museum layout now displays Roman art, medieval weapons, and papal artifacts.

art.description: A bronze statue of Saint Michael holding his sword, created by Peter Anton von Verschaffelt in 1753, stands atop the castle.
A marble statue of Saint Michael by Raffaello da Montelupo, erected in 1536, is located in an interior court.
The original golden quadriga that once crowned the mausoleum.
